title: Airlines and instruments
summary: Hinton on airline treatment; Maxwell's Tonight Show trick.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: There's so many things I want to talk to you about concerning listening. I know it's part of your philosophy as a musician. The discourtesy that's extended me -- not you, because you're a trumpet player. Musicians on airlines, they just treat you like you're so much dirt. And I'm a bass player, you know I catch it. Cello players and violin players, they -- there's no courtesy. There's no simple reason for them to treat us the way they do. If you buy a seat for the bass, they get angry when they see you coming, even when you have a seat. If you have a case like I do, the skycaps all are looking at you like you're bringing a herd of elephant along.
You've got to put out a little effort. Nobody wants to put out any effort.

But they'll be so courteous with all your golfclubs, no matter how big they are, bicycles, skis, anything. And yet musicians are traveling all the time, spending all this money for us to be going. Here we sit here and when both of us land in New York City -- here we are sitting talking about this in New Orleans, Louisiana. And yet,

George Wein spent quite a bundle coming down here, bringing all these musicians down here. But nobody would say, look, I'm sending these musicians, spending thousands and hundreds of thousands of dollars a year, treat them with some respect. Nobody does that.

Well, sometimes I would get treated with respect, and the way that worked was I'd say, "I'm on the 'Tonight Show'" and all of a sudden, everything was great. I would get off the plane and they would get a few tickets for that show.

So there must be something going on, these businessmen with their credit cards and they pinch the stewardess on the butt or something, take them all out, buy them a lot of drinks and show them around town. And musicians are going to take care of business.
